title: Motorcycle, Dirt Bike & Powersport Insurance: The Complete Rider's Guide (Laws, Coverage & Costs)
description: Motorcycle, dirt bike, ATV and bicycle insurance explained: which states require it, what theft and crash cover pays, real costs and the traps to avoid.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: Almost every US state requires [motorcycle insurance](/learn/motorcycle-dirt-bike-powersport-insurance/) for street-registered bikes. Florida is the big exception: see [do you need insurance on a motorcycle in Florida](/qa/do-you-need-insurance-on-a-motorcycle-in-florida/).

Liability-only policies never pay for your own bike. Theft, fire and vandalism are covered only if you add comprehensive. That's the whole answer to [does motorcycle insurance cover theft](/qa/does-motorcycle-insurance-cover-theft/).

Off-road machines (dirt bikes, motocross bikes, ATVs and quads) usually don't need insurance on private land. Several states still require it on public trails or once the vehicle is registered. Check [what states require dirt bike insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/).

Homeowners policies usually exclude motorized vehicles once they leave your property, so a separate [dirt bike insurance](/learn/dirt-bike-insurance-coverage/) or [ATV insurance](/learn/quad-bike-atv-insurance/) policy is often the only real protection.

Minimum-liability motorcycle cover can cost as little as about $10 a month in states like [Colorado](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-colorado/) and [Ohio](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-ohio/). Full coverage on a sport bike for a young rider can cost 5 to 10 times that.

faqs.question: Is motorcycle insurance required in every state?
faqs.answer: No, but almost. Nearly every state requires liability insurance on a street-registered motorcycle. Florida doesn't require riders to show insurance to register a bike, but it enforces financial responsibility after an injury crash and requires $10,000 in medical benefits for helmetless riders over 21. See [do you need insurance on a motorcycle in Florida](/qa/do-you-need-insurance-on-a-motorcycle-in-florida/).

faqs.question: Does my car insurance cover my motorcycle?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Personal auto policies define a covered vehicle as a private passenger vehicle with four wheels, so motorcycles need their own policy or a motorcycle endorsement. Many insurers do offer a multi-policy discount when you bundle them. Check your wording with [how to read an insurance policy](/learn/how-to-read-an-insurance-policy/). See [motorcycle insurance vs car insurance](/compare/motorcycle-insurance-vs-car-insurance).

faqs.question: Do I need insurance for a dirt bike I only ride on my own land?
faqs.answer: Most states don't legally require it on private land. Your homeowners policy may still exclude injuries and damage involving the bike. See [do dirt bikes need insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/) and [dirt bike insurance coverage](/learn/dirt-bike-insurance-coverage/).

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to insure a motorcycle?
faqs.answer: Carry your state's minimum liability on a low-cc cruiser or standard bike, choose a higher deductible, complete a rider safety course, and use a seasonal lay-up option if you store the bike in winter. Don't cut UM/UIM or liability below what your savings need. The [coverage gap checker](/coverage-gap-checker/) helps you find that floor.

faqs.question: Is bicycle insurance worth it if I have renters insurance?
faqs.answer: It depends on the bike's value and your deductible. A renters policy covers theft minus the deductible, so it works for a $3,000 bike on a $250 deductible. It works poorly for a $1,200 bike on a $1,000 deductible, and it rarely covers crash damage. The full breakdown is in [bicycle insurance](/learn/bicycle-insurance/).

content.text: A motorcycle has no crumple zones, no airbags and no roof, so it carries more risk per mile than any car. [NHTSA](https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/motorcycles) reports that in 2024, per vehicle mile traveled, motorcyclists were almost 27 times more likely than passenger car occupants to die in a crash and almost 5 times more likely to be injured. That's why **motorcycle insurance** works differently from a standard [car insurance policy](/learn/car-insurance-guide/). The bike is cheaper to insure against damage, but the medical and liability exposure in a crash is far larger. The same goes for the rest of the two-wheel and powersport family: dirt bikes, motocross bikes, ATVs, quad bikes and even high-end mountain bikes. This hub explains which of these vehicles legally need cover, what each type of policy actually pays, and what riders really spend. Each section links to a detailed answer.

If you're new to how policies are built, start with [how insurance works](/learn/how-does-insurance-work/) and the difference between [coverage and limits](/learn/coverage-vs-limits/). Then come back here to apply it to two wheels, four knobby tires or a pedal-powered carbon frame.
The Powersport Family: What Needs Which Kind of Insurance?

Insurers sort vehicles by where they're allowed to operate. Anything registered for public roads falls under your state's compulsory liability laws. Off-road-only machines usually fall outside them. Pedal bikes are treated as personal property. Use this table to find your vehicle and the guide that covers it:

rows: Required in nearly every state (Florida is a partial exception)
Only on public land or once road-registered, in certain states
Required in some states (e.g. Pennsylvania off your own land)
Rarely state-mandated, often required by lenders/marinas

content.text: Is Motorcycle Insurance Legally Required?

In almost every state, yes. If a motorcycle is registered for public roads, the owner must carry at least the state's minimum **bodily injury and property damage liability**. The minimums vary widely. [Colorado requires 25/50/15](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-colorado/) ($25,000 per person, $50,000 per accident and $15,000 property damage). [Ohio requires 25/50/25](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-ohio/) under its financial-responsibility law. **Florida** is the famous outlier. Motorcycles are left out of its PIP no-fault system, and riders don't have to show insurance to register a bike. But an uninsured rider who causes an injury crash faces financial-responsibility penalties, and helmetless riders over 21 must carry at least $10,000 in medical benefits. The full breakdown is in [do motorcycles need insurance in Florida](/qa/do-you-need-insurance-on-a-motorcycle-in-florida/).

A related question comes up all the time: [can you get motorcycle insurance without a license](/qa/can-you-get-motorcycle-insurance-without-a-license/)? Often you can. Owners who hold only a learner's permit, or who store a bike they don't ride, can usually insure it. The catch is who's allowed to ride it and whether a claim will be paid. The same underwriting logic shows up in [getting auto insurance with a suspended license](/qa/can-you-get-auto-insurance-with-a-suspended-license/) and in [named non-owner policies](/qa/what-is-a-named-non-owner-car-insurance-policy/).

content.title: Riding Uninsured Is a Balance-Sheet Risk, Not Just a Ticket
content.text: State minimums like $15,000 or $25,000 of property damage rarely cover a serious crash that involves a newer SUV and hospital bills. Once your limit runs out, you are personally liable for the rest. Read [what happens if you crash without insurance](/qa/what-happens-if-you-crash-without-insurance/) and consider raising limits or adding an [umbrella policy](/learn/umbrella-insurance-guide/).
What Motorcycle Insurance Covers: The 8 Building Blocks
A motorcycle policy is modular. You add each coverage separately, and each one answers a different question about who pays:

items: **Bodily injury & property damage liability.** Pays for other people's injuries and property when you're at fault. It's legally required in most states and never pays for your own bike.

**Collision.** Pays to repair or replace your motorcycle after a crash with a vehicle or an object, minus your [deductible](/glossary/deductible/). Test deductible choices with the [car insurance deductible calculator](/car-insurance-deductible-calculator/).

**Comprehensive.** Pays for theft, fire, vandalism, hail, flood and animal strikes. This is the coverage behind [motorcycle theft claims](/qa/does-motorcycle-insurance-cover-theft/). See [comprehensive vs collision](/compare/comprehensive-vs-collision/) for how the two split.
**Uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM).** Pays your injury costs when the at-fault driver has no insurance or too little. It matters more for riders because injuries run higher.
**Medical payments.** Pays medical bills regardless of fault. In Florida this can help satisfy the helmet-exemption medical benefit rule.
**[Custom parts & equipment (CPE)](/glossary/custom-parts-and-equipment-coverage/).** Covers aftermarket exhausts, paint, seats and luggage. Standard policies often cap it at a low amount.
**Riding gear.** Pays to replace helmets, jackets and boots damaged in a covered loss.

**Guest passenger liability & roadside assistance.** Covers injuries to a passenger (see [does motorcycle insurance cover passengers](/qa/does-motorcycle-insurance-cover-passengers/)) and pays for towing when you break down far from home.

content.text: How a total loss is valued matters just as much as which coverages you pick. Most policies pay [actual cash value](/glossary/actual-cash-value/), which means market value after depreciation. Classic and custom bikes are better protected with agreed value. The trade-off works the same way it does for collector cars, covered in [agreed value vs actual cash value](/compare/agreed-value-vs-actual-cash-value-classic-car-insurance).

content.title: Motorcycle Theft Is Rising and Recovery Is Poor
content.text: The [National Insurance Crime Bureau](https://www.nicb.org/news/news-releases/lock-your-bikes-motorcycle-thefts-rise-third-consecutive-year) counted 54,736 motorcycle thefts in 2022, up 7% on 2021. California, Florida and Texas led the list, and thefts peaked in July. Only a little over 40% of stolen bikes are recovered. Without comprehensive coverage, a stolen bike is a total out-of-pocket loss. Here's [how motorcycle theft claims are paid](/qa/does-motorcycle-insurance-cover-theft/).
Off-Road Insurance: Dirt Bikes, Motocross Bikes, ATVs and Quads

Off-road machines fall into a gray zone. Most states don't require insurance on a **dirt bike** or **ATV** ridden only on private land. The rules change on public trails, in state parks and once the vehicle is registered for road use. [Pennsylvania](https://www.pa.gov/services/dcnr/register-or-title-your-atv) requires liability insurance for ATVs ridden on land you don't own or lease. New York requires ATVs to be registered, and liability coverage is generally required off the owner's property. [Colorado](https://cpw.state.co.us/register-off-highway-vehicle) requires OHV registration or a permit to ride on public land. The state-by-state picture is in [do dirt bikes need insurance](/qa/do-dirt-bikes-need-insurance/).

The legal question is only half of it. Many families assume their homeowners policy covers the kids' pit bike or the farm quad. Standard homeowners forms usually [exclude](/glossary/exclusion/) motorized vehicles once they leave the insured premises, and some exclude them everywhere. The full breakdown is in [does homeowners insurance cover ATVs and dirt bikes](/qa/does-homeowners-insurance-cover-atvs-and-dirt-bikes/). Organized racing is excluded almost everywhere. That's why [insurance for motocross bikes](/learn/dirt-bike-insurance-coverage/) and [quad bike insurance](/learn/quad-bike-atv-insurance/) are sold as separate policies. For how exclusions are written, see [what is an exclusion in insurance](/learn/what-is-an-exclusion-in-insurance/).

content.title: Why Off-Road Liability Matters
content.text: The [U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission](https://www.cpsc.gov/Safety-Education/Safety-Education-Centers/ATV-Safety-Information-Center) reports an annual average of more than 800 deaths and roughly 100,000 emergency-room-treated injuries involving off-highway vehicles. If a friend is hurt riding your machine, the medical bills and lawsuit can land on you.
Pedal Power: Bicycle, Mountain Bike and Bike Shop Insurance

**Bicycle insurance** is the highest-volume search in this cluster, and it works differently. Bicycles aren't motor vehicles, so no state requires coverage. E-bikes can be different, though. See [do you need insurance for an electric bike](/qa/do-you-need-insurance-for-an-electric-bike/). According to the [Insurance Information Institute](https://www.iii.org/article/bicycle-safety-and-insurance), a homeowners or renters policy typically covers a stolen bike under personal property, minus your deductible. With a $1,000 deductible and a $1,200 bike, that pays very little. Standalone [mountain bike insurance](/learn/bicycle-insurance/) adds low or zero deductibles, crash damage and race cover. If you own the shop rather than the bike, [bike shop insurance](/learn/bike-shop-insurance/) is a commercial package built on [general liability](/learn/commercial-general-liability-guide/), [product liability](/learn/product-liability-insurance/) and customer-bike (bailee) protection.
How Much Does Motorcycle Insurance Cost?

For the national picture, start with [how much is motorcycle insurance](/learn/average-cost-of-motorcycle-insurance/). Motorcycle premiums swing more than car premiums do, because the kind of bike tells the insurer so much about the risk. Minimum-liability cover for an experienced cruiser rider can cost less than a streaming subscription. Full coverage on a 1,000cc sport bike for a 21-year-old can cost more than the rider's car insurance. Published comparison data shows the spread. [MoneyGeek](https://www.moneygeek.com/insurance/motorcycle/best-cheap-motorcycle-insurance-in-colorado/) puts Colorado minimum coverage at about $117 a year and full coverage at about $567 a year. In Ohio, minimum coverage for many riders is estimated at roughly $115 to $315 a year. Worked examples are in [how much is motorcycle insurance in Colorado](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-colorado/) and [how much is motorcycle insurance in Ohio](/qa/how-much-is-motorcycle-insurance-in-ohio/).

rows: Largest single factor. [IIHS](https://www.iihs.org/topics/motorcycles) finds supersport riders die at roughly 4 times the rate of cruiser and standard riders, and premiums reflect it
High. See [how long an accident stays on your insurance](/qa/how-long-does-an-accident-stay-on-your-insurance/)

content.title: Three Fast Ways to Cut Your Motorcycle Premium
content.text: 1) Take a certified rider course. Many insurers discount it, and the [Motorcycle Safety Foundation](https://msf-usa.org/) lists courses nationwide. 2) Ask for seasonal [lay-up coverage](/glossary/lay-up-coverage/), which is often cheaper than dropping cover completely (read [can you pause car insurance](/qa/can-you-pause-car-insurance/) before you cancel anything). 3) Drop collision on an older bike once its value is less than about 10 times the annual collision premium.
7 Powersport Insurance Traps That Cost Riders Thousands

items: **Assuming liability covers theft.** It doesn't, on cars or bikes. Read [does liability insurance cover theft](/qa/does-liability-insurance-cover-theft/).

**Letting an unlicensed rider borrow the bike.** Many policies exclude or limit claims when the operator has no valid motorcycle license. See [motorcycle insurance without a license](/qa/can-you-get-motorcycle-insurance-without-a-license/).
**Under-declaring custom parts.** A $6,000 exhaust-and-paint package on a policy with a $3,000 CPE cap leaves $3,000 unpaid.
**Relying on homeowners for a dirt bike or quad.** Off-premises motorized-vehicle exclusions are standard. Buy [dirt bike insurance](/learn/dirt-bike-insurance-coverage/) instead.

**Racing on a recreational policy.** Timed events and motocross competitions are routinely excluded. You'd need track or event cover. See [event liability insurance](/learn/event-liability-insurance/).

**Letting coverage lapse over winter.** A lapse can raise your renewal price and, in some states, trigger registration penalties. Read [what happens when insurance expires](/learn/what-happens-when-insurance-expires/).
**Choosing liability-only on a bike you can't afford to lose.** Weigh [full coverage vs liability-only motorcycle insurance](/compare/full-coverage-vs-liability-only-motorcycle-insurance) first.
**Skipping UM/UIM to save a few dollars.** Rider injuries run far higher than car injuries. Pay special attention in low-minimum states like Florida and Colorado.
